criteria.description: The summary preserves the original goal and complete acceptance semantics rather than only the most recent implementation slice.
The summary preserves authoritative requirements and accepted decisions, and does not elevate web notes, legacy comments, or rejected proposals into current authority.
The summary distinguishes accepted decisions, open hypotheses, and explicitly rejected approaches.
The summary does not overstate verified evidence or mark unfinished work complete.
Two summaries are equivalent when they preserve the same authoritative facts, state, uncertainty, and next action.
